facts.claim: Malaysia Airports traces its origin to 1991, when Parliament passed legislation separating the Department of Civil Aviation into a regulator and a newly created airport operator, Malaysia Airports Berhad.
facts.notes: PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - not re-confirmed in this run (official sites were blocked and the search budget ran out). Verify against the official source before publishing. Wording follows the long-standing corporate profile text; verify at the official 'Our Profile' page (https://www.malaysiaairports.com.my/about-us/corporate-profile/our-profile), which appeared in search results but could not be opened.

facts.claim: Malaysia Airports Berhad was licensed by the Minister of Transport as the airport operator in November 1992.

facts.claim: Under the privatisation plan, Khazanah Nasional was to hold 40% and the EPF 30%, giving Malaysian institutions 70%, with GIP and ADIA together holding the remaining 30%.

sources.title: PM: No sale of MAHB to foreign firms, ownership boosted to 70pct (NST, June 2024)

facts.notes: CONFLICT/CAVEAT: most reports describe 40/30/30 as the effective stakes in MAHB after the deal (PM quoted: local ownership 'boosted to 70pct'); some early reports describe the same split as stakes within the consortium. Reported split of the foreign 30%: GIP about 25% effective, ADIA about 5% effective. These are planned stakes reported in mid-2024; the final post-completion percentages were not confirmed from an official 2025-2026 source.
